standard.title: Select, justify, test and make designed solutions
standard.description: select, justify, test and use suitable technologies, skills and processes, and apply safety procedures to safely make designed solutions
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can select, justify and use suitable materials, components, tools, equipment and techniques safely (AC9TDE8P03). They have experience with safe production practices. They have not yet worked with full production independence, adapted processes to unforeseen challenges, or experimented with innovative material combinations at this level.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students select, justify, test and use suitable technologies, skills and processes with independence and appropriate safety procedures to safely make designed solutions — including adapting processes to risks and unforeseen challenges.

nodes.label: Independent and safe production practice
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can set up and use tools, equipment and techniques independently and safely, applying appropriate personal protective equipment and safe working practices for the specific design project.
nodes.minimum_width: Independently set up and use at least one tool or piece of equipment relevant to the design project; demonstrate appropriate safe working practices without supervision prompts.
nodes.typical_width: Demonstrate independent safe working practice across the production process — including selecting and setting up equipment appropriately, wearing appropriate PPE, identifying hazards in the production process, and applying risk-reduction strategies without prompting.
wider: Independently set up a specific machine (e.g. lathe) to produce a part to specified dimensions — explain each setup step and the safety rationale for each
Review production safety for a group project and identify risks for each team member's role — develop safety protocols for the shared production environment

response_modes.reason: Safe production practice is procedural and requires sufficient hands-on repetition to become genuinely independent. Students who have only observed or worked with close supervision are not yet operating independently. Practice in context-specific setups (the actual tools and materials of the project) is the path to independence.

success_criteria: Sets up and operates at least one tool or piece of equipment independently
Applies appropriate safe working practices without being prompted
nodes.hinge_reason: Independent safe production is prerequisite for N2 — students who cannot operate tools and equipment safely and independently cannot conduct the experimental material combinations that N2 requires without constant supervision, which prevents genuine experimentation.

nodes.label: Experimenting with material combinations
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can experiment with combinations and manipulation of traditional and contemporary materials, components, tools and techniques, and evaluate their findings.
nodes.minimum_width: Experiment with at least two ways of using or combining a material or technique; record findings and explain which approach was more effective and why.
nodes.typical_width: Experiment with innovative combinations of materials, components and techniques — including contemporary and traditional materials; record findings collaboratively; debate the merits of different approaches with peers; consider sustainability in material choice (e.g. materials that store carbon or reduce demand for less sustainable alternatives).
wider: Experiment with food prepared three different ways to maximise colour, flavour and nutritive value — evaluate which approach best meets the design criteria for a specific food solution
Investigate how a traditional material (e.g. timber) performs compared to a manufactured alternative for a specific application — test for relevant properties and make a justified selection
Experiment with a combination of materials not previously used together — document findings in a shared space and evaluate the combination against the design requirements

response_modes.reason: Material combination judgements develop through accumulated experimental experience — a single combination test does not provide the comparative base needed to evaluate merits. Multiple experiments across different material types build the experiential repertoire that meaningful evaluation requires.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Material combination experiments with documentation and peer debate are rich — students who share findings and argue for different approaches develop deeper understanding than those who work only with their own results.
success_criteria: Experiments with at least two material or technique approaches
Records findings in enough detail that the experiment could be replicated
Evaluates which approach better meets the design requirements and why

nodes.label: Adapting production to risks and challenges
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and respond to risks, unexpected challenges and opportunities that arise during production, modifying processes to maintain quality and sustainability.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one risk or unexpected challenge that arose or could arise during production; describe how you responded or would respond to maintain quality or safety.
nodes.typical_width: Monitor production for risks and unexpected challenges (material faults, workload coordination issues, changed conditions); respond by modifying production processes appropriately; maintain a record of adaptations made and explain the reasoning behind each; maximise sustainability in choices made under constraint.
wider: Document and reflect on a production adaptation made in response to an unforeseen challenge (e.g. material fault, unexpected cooking result) — evaluate whether the adaptation maintained quality and what you would do differently
Plan contingencies for identified production risks before production begins — implement contingency procedures when a risk materialises and evaluate their effectiveness
Analyse how bulk food production introduces coordination and scaling challenges — experiment with adapting a recipe for bulk production and evaluate the impact on quality and safety
success_criteria: Identifies at least one specific production risk or challenge
Describes a specific adaptation made or proposed — not just a general safety principle
